# stripe_billing_meter (Resource)

Defines how usage events are aggregated into a billable quantity. `terraform destroy` deactivates the meter, because Stripe cannot delete one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_billing_meter" "api_calls" {
  display_name = "API calls"
  event_name   = "api_call"

  default_aggregation = {
    formula = "sum"
  }

  customer_mapping = {
    type              = "by_id"
    event_payload_key = "stripe_customer_id"
  }

  value_settings = {
    event_payload_key = "value"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `default_aggregation` (Attributes) The default settings to aggregate a meter's events with. Changing it replaces the resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_aggregation))
- `display_name` (String) The meter’s name. Not visible to the customer.
- `event_name` (String) The name of the meter event to record usage for. Corresponds with the `event_name` field on meter events. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `customer_mapping` (Attributes) Fields that specify how to map a meter event to a customer. Changing it replaces the resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--customer_mapping))
- `event_time_window` (String) The time window which meter events have been pre-aggregated for, if any. Possible values: `day`, `hour`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `value_settings` (Attributes) Fields that specify how to calculate a meter event's value. Changing it replaces the resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--value_settings))

### Read-Only

- `created` (Number) Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the object.
- `livemode` (Boolean) If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
- `status` (String) The meter's status. Possible values: `active`, `inactive`.
- `status_transitions` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--status_transitions))
- `updated` (Number) Time at which the object was last updated. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

<a id="nestedatt--default_aggregation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `default_aggregation`

Required:

- `formula` (String) Specifies how events are aggregated. Possible values: `count`, `last`, `sum`.


<a id="nestedatt--customer_mapping"></a>
### Nested Schema for `customer_mapping`

Required:

- `event_payload_key` (String) The key in the meter event payload to use for mapping the event to a customer.
- `type` (String) The method for mapping a meter event to a customer. Possible values: `by_id`.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--value_settings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `value_settings`

Required:

- `event_payload_key` (String) The key in the meter event payload to use as the value for this meter.

### Nested Schema for `status_transitions`

Read-Only:

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import stripe_billing_meter.api_calls mtr_123
```
